executive_summary: Draw #4974 is a genuinely volatile coupon with no game meriting above 0.80 confidence — this should be flagged as a difficult week. The clearest signals come from xG regression (Middlesbrough massively unlucky, Preston massively lucky) and form divergence (Brentford vs a dysfunctional Aston Villa, Brighton's UP-FORM against a leaky Sunderland). The structured injury data is uniformly empty for all 13 matches, leaving us reliant on Perplexity previews throughout — that absence of verified absences adds a layer of uncertainty to every selection. The coupon's best strategy is disciplined doubling rather than hunting for singles that aren't truly there.
value_radar: Game 9 (Middlesbrough vs Wolverhampton): Boro's xGF of 2.41 against actual goals of 1.0 per game is one of the sharpest xG regression signals on the coupon. At odds of 2.20 for the home win, with strong home form and a promotion-race atmosphere, Boro look undervalued by a market that sees only raw results.

Game 3 (Aston Villa vs Brentford): The odds are level at 2.65 each, yet Aston Villa's xGF of 1.00 per game — the lowest on the entire coupon — and back-to-back home defeats point strongly away from the home side. Brentford at 2.65 to win away represents genuine value against a Villa side that is genuinely broken in attack.

Game 11 (Sheffield United vs Lincoln): Lincoln's away record (three wins in their last four away games) is exceptional for a League One/Championship side and is completely ignored by the 3.85 away price. Sheffield United's defence has conceded 2.5 actual goals per game at home despite an xGA of only 1.62 — a dangerous combination when facing a side on a travelling winning streak.
